*Task 1: Time series bootstrap and the ladle estimator*
```{r}
setting1=function(nobs){
  x1=arima.sim(model = list(ar=0.6, ma=c(0,-0.4)), n=nobs)
  #but the paper tells us that in the SOS model E(z_t)=0 and Cov(z_t)=I. For every variable x1,...,x5 we already
  #have E(x)=0 and cov between every x =0, but we need V(x)=1.We use the theoretical variance
  var1=sum(c(1,ARMAtoMA(ar=0.6,ma=c(0,-0.4),lag.max = 1000))^2)
  x1=x1/sqrt(var1)
  x2=arima.sim(model = list(ar=c(0.4,0.1,0.3), ma=c(0.2,0.4)), n=nobs)
  var2=sum(c(1,ARMAtoMA(ar=c(0.4,0.1,0.3),ma=c(0.2,0.4),lag.max = 1000))^2)
  x2=x2/sqrt(var2)
  x3=arima.sim(model = list(ar=0.4), n=nobs)
  var3=1/(1-0.4^2)
  x3=x3/sqrt(var3)
  x4=arima.sim(model = list(ma=c(0.5,0.3,0.1,0.2)), n=nobs)
  var4=1+sum(c(0.5,0.3,0.1,0.2)^2)
  x4=x4/sqrt(var4)
  x5=arima.sim(model = list(ar=c(0.1,0.1,0.3)), n=nobs)
  var5=sum(c(1,ARMAtoMA(ar=c(0.1,0.1,0.3),lag.max = 1000))^2)
  x5=x5/sqrt(var5)
  x6=rnorm(nobs)
  x7=rnorm(nobs)
  x8=rnorm(nobs)
  x9=rnorm(nobs)
  x10=rnorm(nobs)
  setting1=cbind(x1,x2,x3,x4,x5,x6,x7,x8,x9,x10)
  setting1
}
set.seed(123)
x <- setting1(1000)
```


**part A**

```{r}
library(readr)
#View(x)
#We find the mean of each variable
mean_x <- apply(x, 2, mean)
#We center data by removing the mean of each variable
xc <- sweep(x,2, mean_x, "-")
#We will now find the sample covariance matrix. with the sample correction(n-1)
cov_xc <- cov(xc)
#We follow the paper and whiten using symmetric square root. #We will use svd to decompose the matrix
#SVD decompose cov_xc = U D V^T. Since cov_xc is symmetric and positive definite, U = V = Q is an orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors and D = Lambda
#is a diagonal matrix
s <- svd(cov_xc)
Lambda <- s$d
Q <- s$u
Lambda_inv_sqrt <- diag(1 / sqrt(Lambda))
Lambda_inv_sqrt
WZCA <- Q %*% tcrossprod(Lambda_inv_sqrt, Q)
WZCA
#Whitening data
xw <- xc %*% WZCA
#we will devide by n-tau
#We do up to 12 lags for autocorrelationon
apply(xw, 2, mean)
cov_xw <-cov(xw)
cov_tab <- formatC(cov_xw, format = "e", digits = 2)
diag(cov_tab) <- "1"
dimnames(cov_tab) <- list(paste0("$X_{", 1:10, "}$"), paste0("$X_{", 1:10, "}$"))
#Translate the table to R for reporting
latex_tab <- knitr::kable(cov_tab, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
                          align = "r", escape = FALSE,
                          caption = "Sample covariance of the whitened data")
cat(latex_tab)
# in the paper they test up to 12 lags
taus <- 1:12 
#array that contain the auto covariance
p <- ncol(xw)
acm <- array(0,dim = c(p,p,length(taus)))
#Since the data is centered we should not subtract the mean when calculating the covariance as it is 0. This is only the case as we would have chosen to substract the whole mean
autoc <- function(data, tau){
n <- nrow(data)
1/(n-tau) * crossprod(data[1:(n - tau), ],data[(tau + 1):n, ])
}
for (k in seq_along(taus)){
  acm[,,k] <- autoc(xw,taus[k])
}
```

**Part B**

```{r}
#First think ob B_ib as a block consisting og b observations from x starting from X_i. In the case where j > N i = j(mod N) and X_0 = X_N. Hence we look at data as being circular. 
#fix a number p in 0 to 1
#Make a sequence of iid random variables L independent of X. With prob of L_i = m bing 1 − p)^(m−1) · p for m = 1,2...
#Independent of X_i and L_1 make I_1,I_2,... seq of iid var with discrete uniform dist on {1,..,N}
#We now generate X_1*,...,X_N*. The first block is B_{I_1,L_1} such that X*_1 = X_{I1},... X*_{L_1} = X_{I_1 + #L_1-1} and the pseudo-time series finish once we have N observations.
# For the fixed bootstrap the length of a block is the tuning param, and for stationary bootstrap the probablity p is the tuning param. 

fixed_boot <- function(x,l){
  n=nrow(x)
  nvar=ncol(x)
  m=ceiling(n/l) #for example if we have n=105 and l=20 it gives m=6
  block=matrix(rep(0,m*l*nvar), nrow =m*l )#so that we can sample whole blocks
  j=1
  for (i in 1:m) {
    star=sample(1:(n-l+1), size=1) 
    block[j:(j+l-1),]=x[star:(star+(l-1)),]
    j=j+l
  }
  block[1:n, ]#we just want the first n observations (that can be less than m*l)
}

stationary_boot <- function(x,prob){
  n=nrow(x)
  nvar=ncol(x)
  stationary=matrix(rep(0,n*nvar), nrow =n )
  #We repeat the data for it to emulate circular data
  x2=matrix(rep(0,n*nvar*2), nrow=n*2)
  x2[1:n,]=x
  x2[(n+1):(2*n),]=x
  star=sample(1:n, size=1)
  stationary[1,]=x2[star,]
  for (i in 2:n) {
    #we use runif to decide the length of each block
    if (runif(1)>=prob) {
      star=star+1
      stationary[i,]=x2[star,]
    } else {
      star=sample(1:n, size=1)
      stationary[i,]=x2[star,]
    }
  }
  stationary
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)
B <- 500
#Build the whitning into a function to use for the rest of the code
Get_white <- function(x){
  mean_x <- apply(x, 2, mean)
xc <- sweep(x,2, mean_x, "-")
cov_xc <- cov(xc)
s <- svd(cov_xc)
Lambda <- s$d
Q <- s$u
Lambda_inv_sqrt <- diag(1 / sqrt(Lambda))
WZCA <- Q %*% tcrossprod(Lambda_inv_sqrt, Q)
#Whitening data
xw <- xc %*% WZCA
#Check that the whitened data has identity covariance
err <- max(abs(cov(xw) - diag(ncol(x))))
if (err > 1e-8) stop("Whitening failed", signif(err, 3))
xw
}
```

**Part C**

```{r}
library(JADE)
#We use simplify = "array" such that sapply returns a pxpxK matrix. We increase maxiter and lower the critia of convergence to achieve convergence
acf_rjd <- function(data, taus) {
  rjd(sapply(taus, function(tau) autoc(data, tau), simplify = "array"),eps = 1e-5, maxiter = 1500)
}

Get_U <- function(xw, Taus){
  #We do the joint diagonilzation with rjd on the whitend data, which returns the diagnolizer U and the approximate diagonalized AC 
  rjd <- acf_rjd(xw,Taus)
  U <- rjd$V
  d <- apply(rjd$D,3, diag)
  #We then sum over the lag set to optain the diagnoal matrix. Idea is to sum all lags^2 for each variable, the result is a vector
  lambda_diag <- rowSums(d^2) 
  #Order Lambda from largest to smallest
  ord <- order(lambda_diag, decreasing = TRUE)
  lambda_diag_ord <- lambda_diag[ord]
  #We then order the diagonal from largest to smallest and U such that it match lambda_diag_ord
  U_ord <- U[,ord]
  list(U =U_ord, Lambda = lambda_diag_ord)
}



f_replicate <- function(x, U_org, Taus,b, stationary = TRUE){
  p <- ncol(U_org)
  #We do either fixed or stationary (default) bootstrap
  xs <- if (stationary) stationary_boot(x, 1/b) else fixed_boot(x, b)
  xws <- Get_white(xs)
  #We find U from one bootstrap sample
  U_star <- Get_U(xws,Taus)$U
  sapply(1:(p - 1), function(k) {
    #Drop false keeps the structure of the matrix
    B_hat <- U_org[,1:k, drop = FALSE]
    B_star <- U_star[,1:k, drop = FALSE]
    1 - abs(det(crossprod(B_hat,B_star)))})
}

f_k_func <- function(x,U,Taus,b,B, stationary = TRUE){
  #we first get all the det for the sum over all bootstrap samples, by replicating B 1 - abs(det)
  f <- replicate(B, {
  f_replicate(x, U, Taus,b, stationary)
  })
  #We then sum over the det and and 0 as the first value
  f_0 <- c(0, rowMeans(f))
  f_0_sum <- sum(f_0)
  #We then get the vector of all the normalized f_k values
  f_k <- f_0 / (1 + f_0_sum)
  f_k
}
g <- function(x, Taus,b,B, stationary = TRUE){
  #Get U and lambda from the original sample
  xw <- Get_white(x)
  res_org <- Get_U(xw, Taus)
  #find f
  f_k <- f_k_func(x, res_org$U,Taus,b,B, stationary)
  lambda <- res_org$Lambda
  #find phi
  phi <- lambda / (1 + sum(lambda))
  #find g
  g_k <- f_k + phi
  list(f = f_k, phi = phi, g = g_k, q_hat = which.min(g_k) - 1)
}

```

**Part D**
First we will try to recreate the resuls from figure 1

Both plots look similar, and have the same conclution. They are also in agreement with the result of figure one from the article

```{r}
set.seed(123)
#Amount of independent datasets we will simualte for each time series (paper uses 2000)
R <- 100
#Amount of bootsrap samples within each ladle
B <- 100
#n is the length of the simulated series. The guess is that a longer series will improve the result
ns <-c(200, 500, 1000,1500)
#Length of block or expected length of block depending on bootstrap method
bs <- c(5,10, 20, 30,50)
results <- data.frame()
for (n in ns) {
  for (r in 1:R) {
    print(r)
  #Simulate data of length n. When we are making a new simulation instead always bootstraping from the same simulation we are removing the chance of the dataset lucky/unlucky for getting the correct value of 5. Hence this actually tells about the methods real performance of data with this type of distribution. I want to discuss with Andrea wether this is a hard data to replicate
  x <- setting1(n)
    for (b in bs) {
      #boptstrap with both fixed and stationary and extract q
      q_F <- g(x, 1:12, b,B, FALSE)$q_hat
      q_S <- g(x, 1:12, b, B)$q_hat
      results <-rbind(results, data.frame(n = n, method = c("F", "S"), b = b, q_hat = c(q_F, q_S)))
    }
  }
}

```
```{r}
#Build sumamry table
summary_q <- data.frame()
mcse_q <- data.frame()
for(n in ns){
  for( m in c("F", "S")){
    for(b in bs){
      #Find q for the combination of sample size, method and block length
      q <- results$q_hat[results$n == n & results$method == m & results$b == b]
      counts <- numeric(10)
      #summary
      #count how many q's fell into each possible outcome
      for(i in 1:10){
        counts[i] <-sum(q == (i-1))
      }
      #Converge to percentage (not nessary for R = 100)
      perc <- 100 * counts /length(q)
      summary_q <- rbind(summary_q, data.frame(n = n, method = m, b = b, t(perc)))
      #MCSE we know the true value is 5
      I <- q == 5
      #How many q turn out to be the true mean
      p_hat <- mean(I)
      R <- length(q)
      mcse <- sd(I) / sqrt(R)
      mcse_q <- rbind(mcse_q, data.frame(n =n, method =m, b = b,p = p_hat, MCSE = mcse, lower_bound = p_hat - 1.96 * mcse, upper_bound =p_hat + 1.96 * mcse ))
    }
  }
}
colnames(summary_q) <- c("n", "method", "b", paste0("q=", 0:9))
summary_q
#Not sure yet if it makes sense to include the MCSE
mcse_q
```

  for( m in c("F", "S")){
    for(b in bs){
      #Find q for the combination of sample size, method and block length
      q <- results_sf$q_hat[results_sf$n == n & results_sf$method == m & results_sf$b == b]
      counts <- numeric(10)
      #summary
      #count how many q's fell into each possible outcome
      for(i in 1:10){
        counts[i] <-sum(q == (i-1))
      }
      #Converge to percentage (not nessary for R = 100)
      perc <- 100 * counts /length(q)
      summary_sf <- rbind(summary_sf, data.frame(n = n, method = m, b = b, t(perc)))
      #MCSE we know the true value is 5
      I <- q == 5
      #How many q turn out to be the true mean
      p_hat <- mean(I)
      R <- length(q)
      mcse <- sd(I) / sqrt(R)
      mcse_sf <- rbind(mcse_sf, data.frame(n =n, method =m, b = b,p = p_hat, MCSE = mcse, lower_bound = p_hat - 1.96 * mcse, upper_bound =p_hat + 1.96 * mcse ))
    }
  }
}
colnames(summary_sf) <- c("n", "method", "b", paste0("q=", 0:9))
summary_sf
#Not sure yet if it makes sense to include the MCSE
mcse_sf
```

```{r}

sensitivityanalysis <- do.call(rbind, lapply(bs, function(b){
  data.frame(b =b, StationaryBootstrap = replicate(r,g(x, 1:12, b, B)$q_hat), FixedBootstrap = replicate(r,g(x, 1:12, b, B, FALSE)$q_hat))
}))
table(sensitivityanalysis$b, sensitivityanalysis$StationaryBootstrap)
table(sensitivityanalysis$b, sensitivityanalysis$FixedBootstrap)
